cloudflare-dns.description: Manages DNS records for the homelab's own domains via the Cloudflare API. Used to stand up a public hostname for a new self-hosted service, or to check and fix an existing record.
when: Adding DNS for a service that just went live on the homelab
Checking whether a hostname's record already exists before creating a duplicate
Verifying a record actually propagated and the TLS proxy picked it up

r620-deploy.description: End-to-end workflow for shipping a .NET service to the homelab's Docker Swarm host: build a real image, register the stack, deploy it, and verify a live TLS endpoint rather than just "container is running."
when: Standing up a brand-new homelab service for the first time
Redeploying an existing service after a code change
Chasing down why a deploy looks fine but is silently serving stale data or the wrong TLS cert

r620-remote-ops.description: Operates the homelab's Docker Swarm host safely from a sandboxed session where direct SSH to the LAN isn't reachable, by going through the container platform's HTTPS API instead.
when: A background/sandboxed session needs to read service state but the LAN IP is blocked
A low-risk service operation (restart, one-shot exec) needs to happen without a foreground session

keycloak-admin.description: Manages a self-hosted Keycloak identity server — realms, clients, users, and role mappings — through its Admin REST API instead of the admin console UI.
when: A new app needs an OIDC client registered for login
Inspecting or fixing realm config, users, or role assignments

seq.description: Queries the homelab's centralized structured-log server over its HTTP API.
when: Checking application logs for a specific service or error
Verifying a newly deployed service is actually emitting logs
Debugging a production issue without SSHing in to grep raw files

stack-apply.description: Reconciles a Docker Swarm stack's compose definition against what's actually running on the homelab host in one atomic pass — refuses to deploy secret-shaped env literals or a TLS router missing its cert resolver, and diffs against live state rather than trusting a possibly-stale git copy.
when: Pushing a compose.yml change to an existing self-hosted stack
Anything beyond piecemeal, hand-edited service updates

secret-apply.description: Generates or accepts one new secret value and applies it everywhere it needs to land — env files, CI secrets, a secrets manager — in a single hands-off pass. Self-issued secrets (DB passwords, keys) generate non-interactively; provider-issued credentials (PATs, OAuth tokens) are taken once via a GUI or hidden prompt. Never surfaces the value to a transcript, shell history, or process list.
when: A new service needs a credential minted and wired into every place it's consumed
Rotating an existing secret across env files, CI, and a secrets manager at once

twitch-api.description: Works with the Twitch Helix API and EventSub for a stream-relay/chatbot and browser-extension project family.
when: Calling Twitch Helix endpoints directly
Debugging a relay service's OAuth/chat connection
Working on the Twitch extension itself

dreadtv-firetv-deploy.description: Sideloads an Android TV app build onto Fire TV devices on the local network via ADB, and checks which known devices are currently reachable and authorized.
when: A new build needs pushing to test devices
Checking which Fire TVs on the LAN are ready to receive a build

batocera-audio.description: Checks and switches the active audio output device (HDMI vs. headphone jack) on a Batocera retro-gaming console over SSH, and remembers which device actually worked per host.
when: Audio cut out after a cable swap
A quick status check before assuming a controller/audio problem is hardware

lan-mouse.description: Diagnoses and fixes lan-mouse (feschber/lan-mouse) cursor-capture problems on a Linux desktop — cursor stuck to a peer, a permission dialog looping, or the daemon fighting for control.
when: LanMouse cursor capture misbehaves and the fix isn't obvious
Instead of re-deriving the same diagnosis from scratch each time

nuget-publish.description: Publishes internal .NET packages to a private NuGet feed so other repos can restore them.
when: A library needs to be versioned and pushed for other repos to consume
Diagnosing a "package not found" or restore failure against the internal feed
